Yes. I found several Toronto/GTA marketers with publicly documented fitness/gym work, plus a couple with particularly relevant gymnastics experience.

Strongest matches

H2O Digital Marketing Inc. — fitness/franchise marketing

Their strongest proof is their Orangetheory case study
.

They started with a small number of Canadian Orangetheory studios and eventually managed paid social for 400+ studios across North America.

Particularly interesting if you're looking for paid ads, lead generation, localized campaigns and multi-location fitness marketing.

The Influence Agency — fitness + experiential/influencer

They have a substantial GoodLife Fitness case study
.

The campaign combined experiential marketing, brand ambassadors, digital marketing and lead generation at Toronto Raptors/Maple Leafs games.

The documented campaign generated 485 contest entries/leads from 675 direct engagements.

Better fit if you want brand, influencer, experiential and digital marketing, rather than just Meta ads.

New Design Group Inc. — gymnastics specifically

This is one of the most directly relevant examples I found.

They worked on Gymalaya, a children's gymnastics business, including its mascot, logo, website and marketing materials. 
New Design Group Inc.

This makes them worth considering if you're specifically looking for someone who understands children's gymnastics + parent-focused marketing/branding, rather than generic fitness.

XMC — sports/experiential

Toronto-based experiential and sponsorship agency.

Their work includes sports, athlete programs, partnerships and digital campaigns. 
XMC

More appropriate for larger organizations, sponsorships and events than a local gymnastics gym needing enrollment leads.

Fitness Studio Marketing Canada — highly specialized in fitness

Their portfolio is unusually relevant: they show a case study for Fitness 365 in Toronto, reporting a 113% increase in organic visitors and 5,000+ leads. 
Fitness Studio Marketing Canada

They also show work for martial arts, yoga and other fitness businesses.

If your priority is getting gym/studio memberships and leads, this is probably one of the first specialists I'd investigate.

TrueCraft Digital Media — boutique fitness branding + website

Their Brightside Athletics case study involved a Toronto boutique fitness studio, specifically focusing on brand identity, membership conversion and a mobile-first booking website. 
True Craft Digital Media

Good fit for rebranding + website + conversion, rather than purely ongoing advertising.

Charming Media — fitness/wellness PR + influencers

Toronto boutique agency with a wellness/fitness focus.

They cite a Toronto fitness-studio opening involving 100+ attendees, influencers, media and VIPs.

More relevant for awareness, PR, influencers and launches than direct-response membership acquisition.

One more worth knowing

MKTG Canada is Toronto-based and specializes in sports/entertainment marketing, but it's a very different type of agency—more large-scale sponsorships, activations and sports properties than marketing a local gymnastics facility.

My shortlist

If you're evaluating these specifically for a gymnastics/fitness business, I'd rank the publicly demonstrated fit roughly:

Agency	Fitness proof	Gymnastics proof	Best for
Fitness Studio Marketing Canada	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐	Leads + memberships
H2O Digital	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐	Paid social + multi-location
New Design Group	⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	Children's gymnastics + branding
TrueCraft	⭐⭐⭐⭐	—	Brand + website + conversions
Influence Agency	⭐⭐⭐⭐	—	Digital + influencers + experiential
Charming Media	⭐⭐⭐	—	PR + influencers + launches

One caveat: I would distinguish between an agency that says it serves fitness and one that can show actual client results. The first five above have substantially more concrete public evidence than a generic “we work with gyms” claim.

If you tell me whether you're looking for (a) more gymnastics registrations/leads, (b) social media/content, (c) Google/Meta ads, or (d) a full rebrand/website, I can narrow this to the best 3 Toronto agencies and compare their actual case studies, pricing signals, reviews, and likely fit.
